summary: Lane County summit lookout near Springfield, built 1934 by a CCC crew; gone by 1970 per register, removed 1971 per history page; no source describes the site today.

facts.design: L-6 tower with a frame cabin, 87 feet per the register and firelookout.com; 79-foot tower built by the Wendling CCC camp per the history page
facts.status_note: Register and firelookout.com say gone by 1970; the history page says the lookout was removed in 1971

staffing.status: lookout on the post in 1942 (Donald McDonald continued after Ronald Byers was transferred); no end date given

facts.agency: Oregon Department of Forestry, Eastern Lane District (history page); Eastern Lane FPA (register and firelookout.com)

events.note: Road to the summit and a lookout house completed by June 1934; the Wendling CCC camp built a 79-foot tower per the history page; register and firelookout.com give 87 feet
Donald McDonald of Marcola to continue at the Nebo lookout after Ronald Byers was transferred
Observation cab found unsafe; materials bought for replacement
Register and firelookout.com say gone by 1970
History page says the lookout was removed in 1971

evidence.supports: 87-foot L-6 tower and frame ground cabin built 1934 and gone by 1970
evidence.quote: Built in 1934, this 87' L-6 tower and frame ground cabin were gone by 1970.

evidence.supports: Eastern Lane FPA administers the site (register: Administered by Eastern Lane FPA)
87-foot L-6 tower and frame cabin, 1934, gone 1970
about 16 miles northeast of Springfield in Lane County
Mount Nebo is in Lane County
79-foot tower built in 1934 by members of the Wendling CCC camp
evidence.quote: 1934: A 79-foot tower constructed by members of the Wendling CCC camp.

evidence.supports: road and lookout house at the top completed by June 1934
evidence.quote: June 19, 1934: A road to the top of Mt. Nebo and a lookout house at the top have just been completed.

evidence.supports: 1933 Samuel L. Miller field report recommended a tower at least 75 feet tall on a long summit with no distinct top
evidence.quote: November 7, 1933 ... The lookout tower should be at least 75 feet in height, as Nebo is in reality a long hogsback with no distinct top. ... Samuel L. Miller Field Report

evidence.supports: September 1942 Eugene Guard item: lookout on the Nebo post; McDonald continues after Byers transferred to Castle Rock
evidence.quote: September 13, 1942: Ronald Byers, engaged as forestry lookout at the Mt. Nebo post, has been transferred to Castle Rock. Donald McDonald of Marcola will continue serving at the Nebo lookout. (The Eugene Guard)

evidence.supports: 1956 district report: observation cab unsafe; materials purchased to replace it
evidence.quote: 1956: The observation cab was found to be deteriorated to the point of being unsafe for use. Materials were purchased and replacement will be done as weather permits.

evidence.supports: history page gives 1971 as the removal year
history page names the Eastern Lane District, Oregon Department of Forestry as the agency
evidence.quote: Eastern Lane District, Oregon Department of Forestry

resolved_conflicts.explanation: History page says 79 feet as built in 1934, and a 1933 report asked for at least 75 feet; register and firelookout.com say 87 feet. The 24.1 m figure (79 feet) is kept from the brief and the 87-foot figure is noted.
Register and firelookout.com say gone by 1970; the history page says removed in 1971. Both dates are recorded as events.
History page names the Eastern Lane District of the Oregon Department of Forestry; register and firelookout.com name the Eastern Lane FPA.

notes_for_editor: The brief says this record shares a register number with another site. The firelookout.com list shows Mount Nebo as US 980 and Nebo Peak in Wallowa County as US 1128, so the shared-number note needs checking. The register photo caption reads 1934 to 1955, which does not match the 1970 and 1971 removal dates, so it is not used. No source describes the summit today or public access, so access is omitted.
